newsitem.title: GERMANY: Firm Bunds seen hostage to U.S. data on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Firm Bunds seen hostage to U.S. data on Tuesday.

text.p: German Bunds rose to strong gains in late trade on Monday in a short-covering rally fuelled by bullish domestic fundamentals including sluggish economic growth and rising unemployment.
March Bund futures closed up 74 basis points at 100.85 just before the close, after reaching a session high of 100.97. The gains were initiated by a recovery in Treasuries late on Friday.
Dealers predicted Bunds would test the 101.00 level but that further strong gains were unlikely ahead of U.S. December consumer price and retail sales data, due Tuesday at 1330 GMT.
"I can imagine we'll test 101, the market looks positive," one Frankfurt-based dealer said.
The 10-year yield spread between Bunds and T-Notes widened to 90 basis points and dealers said the spread may increase further over the coming days.
But they warned that Bunds will be unable to hold on to their gains if Treasuries fall, as feared by market participants who expect Tuesday's CPI data to increase fears of a U.S. credit tightening.
Economists polled by Reuters expect CPI to be up 0.3 percent month-on-month and 3.3 percent year-on-year. They forecast U.S. retail sales up 0.5 percent.
